subject: health
title: Launch and diagnostic: trusted adults and health helpers
essentialQuestion: How do I find information I can trust and use it to make a healthy choice?
materials: paper or a digital tool for an advocacy message
keyPoints: Health helpers include doctors, nurses, dentists, pharmacists, school nurses, and paramedics.
Different helpers do different jobs, so knowing who to ask saves time.
It is fine to ask a health helper questions about your own body and care.
A trusted adult usually helps you reach the right helper.
privacySafeScenario: Who would you ask about a tooth that hurts when you drink something cold, and who would you ask about a cut that will not stop bleeding?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about trusted adults and health helpers to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Name one thing you already knew about trusted adults and health helpers and one question you now have.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about trusted adults and health helpers.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: The advocacy message may be a poster, a spoken message, a letter, an audio note, a slide, or a described plan. No public posting, publication, or performance is required.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about trusted adults and health helpers under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, find out where medicines are stored in your home and why they are kept there. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
